scope: B2wPiper, OFFICIAL ATEC-TaskB-B2wPiper env, single env, camera-free, ORACLE probe. seed 42. NOT the visual policy path.
headline: First delivery point: the official objects_in_circle reward fired.
sequence: settle, then park the base 0.60 m behind the object along the line to the bin
descend the body 0.06 m on solved wheels-planted leg geometry
two-stage reach: arrive above the grasp point, then descend vertically onto it
close the jaws 25 mm PAST the stop, so the position servo keeps pressing
lift: the object leaves the ground and travels with the jaws
carry: drive straight at the bin, since this chassis cannot steer
the held object meets the bin wall and the wheels stall -- that is the cue to raise
raise the object 0.40 m clear of the 0.55 m lip, then drive further in
release: the object falls inside the wall

what_made_delivery_possible.the_target_is_the_bin: TARGET_CENTER (-3,-10) is where task_b/terrain.py builds the trash bin, and the 1.0 m reward radius equals the bin's outer wall radius (bin_diameter 2.0). The wall stands 0.50 m above the bin floor.
what_made_delivery_possible.pushing_alone_cannot_score: An object pushed against the OUTSIDE of the wall has its root at r = 1.0 + its radial half-extent, i.e. 1.02-1.03 m, outside the 1.0 m threshold. It has to go over the lip.
what_made_delivery_possible.the_reward_also_bounds_height: ObjectsInCircle requires 0 <= root z <= 0.5, so an object merely held above the lip does not score. It has to be released and fall inside: the measuring step is the one where it is at r = 0.944 and z = 0.496.
what_made_delivery_possible.this_chassis_cannot_steer: A differential wheel command of +/-1.75 rad/s produced 0.05 rad/s and no yaw change at all -- the wheels stall and the robot spins on nothing. This project reached the same conclusion at F0.8 (differential steering torque insufficient). Only a straight drive is usable, so the park has to line the bin up along the body's forward axis.
what_made_delivery_possible.the_body_must_stay_clear_of_the_bin: base_link is about 0.43 m long and 0.24 m half-wide, so its front corner reaches ~0.49 m ahead of the origin. At 1.484 m from the centre that corner touches the wall: an earlier run tripped illegal_contact at 3.16 N and terminated. The drive now stops at 1.58 m.

defects_found_and_fixed_on_the_way: The jaw axis was pointed along the approach instead of across it, so the fingers closed front-to-back across the bottle's 96 mm side and could not close at all.
The arm's 0.084 rad position-servo sag was unmeasured and uncompensated; an integral trim plus a convergence-gated reach fixed it.
The probe's leg command started at alpha 0, which meant 'return to standing' and silently erased the evaluator's descent within 30 steps.
The front wheel stood on the object: in the descended stance the furthest wheel edge reaches body x 0.563 m. Parking at 0.50 put the object 35 mm inside it.
A single-stage reach raked the finger tips (21 mm beyond the jaw midpoint) across the object's top; the reach is now two-stage and vertical.
A 0.40 m raise commanded at once moved at ~0.57 m/s and threw the object out of the jaws; the place motions are interpolated over 2.5 s.
Raising and moving inward as one IK target exceeded the arm's reach from the real grasp pose; they are now separate targets.
Driving in after the raise, rather than only reaching in, was needed: the arm's inward move achieved 47% of its target.

harnesses.task_b/leg_kinematics.py: B2w leg FK and the wheels-planted vertical solver, frames read from b2w_piper.usda.
harnesses.task_b/grasp_probe.py: The oracle probe policy: reach, close, lift, carry, raise, release.
harnesses.task_b/audit_grasp.py: 27 CPU checks covering the first_reach grasp sequence, the oracle probe, the delivery phases and a static check that the evaluator's policy constructions match the policy signatures. Pass.

not_shown: This is ORACLE-targeted: the evaluator read the object's true pose and supplied the base's true pose, so the probe proves the delivery MECHANICS end to end and earns a genuine official reward. It demonstrates nothing about perception, navigation, or the official visual policy path, and it is one object of one type on one seed. No claim of a policy score is made.
